page.title: Your week
page.purpose: Show a dated seven-day plan so a person can see slots, anchors, locks, and exactly what a replan would change before any write.

priorities.statement: The actual local date range and meal scope are read before any row.
Locked occurrences are unmistakable and survive a replan preview unchanged.
A replan preview shows changed, unchanged, and locked rows against the captured input revision.
Unknown cost, nutrient, or time contributions and infeasible required constraints are named in the summary.
An open or unrecorded slot contributes unknown future intake, never zero or assumed compliance.

states.description: The surface at rest with data present; the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
First read of the page's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
The read succeeded and there is genuinely nothing, which is distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing data could not be read; what is missing is named rather than shown as zero.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
The request failed; the reason and the next available action are stated.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified next to it.
A write is in flight; the affected control says why it is unavailable.
The client cannot reach the API; read-only or queued behavior is explained.
The plan is being read across all configured breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack slots rather than the dinner row alone.
A replan draft is shown with changed, unchanged, and locked rows and a before/after summary, before anything is applied.
A profile, price, recipe, stock, or plan input changed since the preview was generated, so the preview must be rebuilt.
A required rule, appliance, or lock makes a requested occurrence infeasible; the rule is named and required constraints are not relaxed.
The selected preview has been applied against its captured input revision and the plan reflects it.

elements.description: The actual local date range and the active meal scope.
Previous and next week navigation that preserves the selected week across refresh.
Switches between the dinner row and the full configured day without changing the plan.

elements.name: Days
elements.description: The readable day-grouped occurrence list, preferred over a desktop matrix on small screens.
One local date with its slots and occurrences.
Date/slot, meal, servings, metrics, status, and lock state.
A visible lock marker with a text label, not a colour-only cue.

elements.name: Week summary
elements.description: Known portion cost, estimated checkout, active prep, and variety with their denominator.
States which summary contributors are unknown or missing so an average is not read as complete.

elements.name: Replan
elements.description: Requests a draft for the selected week's unlocked future occurrences.

elements.name: Replan preview
elements.description: Changed, unchanged, and locked rows with a before/after summary.
Per-row change classification for the pending draft.
Names the material input that changed and requires a rebuilt preview before apply.
Names the rule or lock that makes an occurrence infeasible and the action that would resolve it.
Marks an intentionally open or unrecorded slot as unknown future intake.

claims.statement: The week page states its actual local date range and active meal scope before the rows.
Every locked occurrence carries a visible lock label rather than a colour-only marker.
A replan preview preserves locked occurrences unchanged and shows them distinctly from changed rows.
When a material input changed, the page states which input is stale and requires a rebuilt preview instead of applying the old one.
The week summary labels the denominator and missing-data status of every average it shows.
An infeasible occurrence names the required rule or lock that blocks it and never trades that rule against cost, effort, or variety.
An open or unrecorded slot is shown as unknown future intake rather than zero or assumed compliance.
Switching from the dinner row to the full configured day is perceivably different and does not silently alter the plan.
In the preview, applying the draft is the one dominant action with keeping the current plan subordinate.
The day-grouped week never scrolls the whole document sideways; wide content is confined to its own region.
After apply, the day list and summary reflect the applied draft so a successful apply cannot be mistaken for a no-op.
